## Wave 2 Summary

Wave 2 is the C10 DILUTION-CC unconditional-discharge cluster — the Volovik tracking-vacuum closure. The substrate IS the Volovik q-theory vacuum: the cosmological constant is the spectral-action **zeroth** moment a₀ (`a_0_FW_zeta = 6440.0`, zeta-regulated), a DIFFERENT spectral moment than gravity (a₂). C10 is currently `ASSUMED-PARTIALLY-PROVEN` in Atlas-04 — the tracking scaling `rho_vac ~ M_Pl² H²` (exponent n=2) is posited at the substrate-IS level (Volovik q-theory `rho_vac(q) = ε(q) − μ q`). The S98 W2 disposition split C10 into a two-layer / three-object structure with **exactly one** remaining object (Object C) gating the OPEN→CLOSED transition of capstone §8.5. Two independent gates close this wave:

- **W2-1 (`S99-W2-RELAXATION-CLOSURE`)** — the single remaining Object-C leg for an UNCONDITIONAL discharge: integrate the substrate cosmological-friction ODE `q″ + 3Hq′ + V′(q)=0` (V(q)=δρ_vac from the 992 D_K eigenfrequencies) along a **NON-degenerate** substrate Hubble backbone H(τ), and test whether the late-time attractor slope `d ln q/d ln H = 1` (⇒ n=2) emerges UNFORCED — WITHOUT imposing the slow-roll quasi-static relation a priori. **HARD-ORDERED after Wave 1** (W1-1): it consumes the re-derived NON-conformally-stationary substrate H(τ) backbone. The S98 V.2 predecessor (`S98-W2-2-RELAXATION-CLOSURE`) closed PRE-REG-INC because the AOFT acoustic frame selected by S98 V.1 is conformally STATIONARY (a_eff const to rel-var 7.4e-7), which degenerates the ratio-form deceleration observable into 0/0; W1-1's express deliverable is a non-stationary H(τ) backbone that W2-1 can integrate against. Only W2-1 moves the C10 tag.

- **W2-2 (`S99-W2-BBN-RELIEF`)** — quantify the additional substrate relief needed to bring the BBN-epoch vacuum fraction to ΔN_eff(vacuum) ≤ 1. S98 V.10 established the from-below n_eff=1.978111 (V.9 pinned, TYPE-A divergence) gives `(rho_vac/rho_rad)_BBN = 0.474049` ⇒ `ΔN_eff = 2.0873` — direction CORRECT (from-below ⇒ suppression) but magnitude insufficient (0.474 > bound 0.227, short by factor ~2.087). W2-2 identifies which additional substrate mechanism (larger from-below shift / epoch-dependent α_V / a distinct dilution channel) closes the residual. **INDEPENDENT of W1-1/W2-1** — it consumes only the S98 V.9 / V.10 outputs and runs regardless of the Wave-1 verdict.

Carry-forward source: `session-98-w2-workingpaper.md §"Carry-Forward Computations"` — CF-S99-W2-RELAXATION-NONSTATIONARY-H [genuine-math] (W2-1) + CF-S99-W2-BBN-ADDITIONAL-RELIEF [genuine-math] (W2-2).

### Wave 1 → Wave 2 Decision Point (W1-1 → W2-1 HARD ORDERING — PRE-REGISTERED)

The relaxation-closure friction ODE `q″ + 3Hq′ + V′(q)=0` consumes the substrate Hubble backbone H(τ). The S98-era AOFT acoustic frame selected by S98 V.1 Clause-1 is conformally STATIONARY — a_eff is constant to rel-var 7.4e-7, so the conformal factor Ω=√(ρ_s/a₂) cancels the bare complexity growth and the ratio-form deceleration q=−a_eff·ä_eff/ȧ_eff² is intrinsically 0/0 (S98 V.1 Clause-2 FAIL; q_central 1.94e7, only 116/999 finite points). **The AOFT acoustic frame therefore CANNOT serve as W2-1's backbone.** W1-1's express deliverable is a re-derived NON-conformally-stationary substrate H(τ) backbone (a non-ratio observable export); W2-1 integrates the friction ODE against THAT backbone. Planning W2-1 against the conformally-stationary frame would re-inherit the very degeneracy W1-1 resolves.

**Decision point (pre-registered, anticipated at plan-authorship time per `mechanical-closure-discipline.md §"When mechanical closure IS acceptable"` item 1 — this is NOT post-hoc plan editing / Class-3):**

- **IF** `S99-W1-Q-NONRATIO-OBSERVABLE` is **PASS** at W2-1 dispatch time (it exported a finite, non-conformally-stationary substrate H(τ) backbone) → W2-1 runs the full friction-ODE attractor computation consuming that H(τ).

- **IF** `S99-W1-Q-NONRATIO-OBSERVABLE` is **FAIL / INFO / UNCOMPUTED** at W2-1 dispatch time → W2-1 honestly closes via **mechanical closure** (the canonical pattern `computations/_shared/s99_w2_pre_reg_inc_closure.py`, pre-authorized HERE): emit `FAIL -- value='PRE-REG-INC_blocked_by_S99-W1-Q-NONRATIO-OBSERVABLE_<status>'`, update the working-paper §W2-1 **Status / Verdict / Results / Substrate framing** blocks IN-SCRIPT in the same run, and route the full W2-1 computation as a `CF-S100` carry-forward conditional on W1-1 landing PASS. Per `mechanical-closure-discipline.md` item 2 the closure verdict is FAIL/PRE-REG-INC, **NEVER PASS**; per item 3 the closure pinmap embeds per-gate identity keys (`_gate_id`, `_wp_id`, `_scheme`, `_convention`) so its `audit_sha256` is distinct from every other line; per item 4 the descriptive `value=` string names the blocking prereq and its status; per item 5 the working-paper update lands in the same run as the verdict-line append. The closure mechanism mirrors the S98 W1→W2 prereq-block that already fired PRE-REG-INC (`S98-W2-2-RELAXATION-CLOSURE: FAIL -- value='PRE-REG-INC_blocked_by_S98-W1-ROUTE-RECONCILIATION_FAIL_AOFT-frame-conformally-stationary_q-attractor-0over0_full-run-CF-S99'`).

The orchestrator at `/rclab-coordinate` time MUST close Wave 1 (W1-1) BEFORE W2-1 dispatches; **W2-2 pipelines independently** and dispatches regardless of the W1-1 / W2-1 outcome (it consumes only the S98 V.9 / V.10 static npz outputs).

**7-field decision-point format (per `.claude/rules/output-standards.md §"Action Items Format"`):**

1. **What**: gate W2-1 dispatch routing on the W1-1 verdict (full friction-ODE run vs PRE-REG-INC mechanical closure).
2. **Who**: orchestrator (at `/rclab-coordinate` time) selects the branch; `transit-dynamics-theorist` (full run) OR the pre-authorized closure script (block branch).
3. **Input**: `S99-W1-Q-NONRATIO-OBSERVABLE` verdict line in `computations/session-99/s99_gate_verdicts.txt`.
4. **Output**: either a full `S99-W2-RELAXATION-CLOSURE` PASS/FAIL/INFO line, or a PRE-REG-INC FAIL closure line + in-script WP §W2-1 update.
5. **Format**: verdict line + dual-SHA companion + `[SIGN]` 3-tuple companion (full run) OR closure verdict line + companion comment row (block branch); WP §W2-1.
6. **Deadline**: Wave 2, after Wave 1 closes.
7. **Depends on**: `S99-W1-Q-NONRATIO-OBSERVABLE` (Wave 1, HARD).

# (7) substitution_chain — mandatory for sign/direction/threshold claims
substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "The friction-ODE late-time attractor slope d ln q/d ln H = 1, set by the substrate
            quadratic V(q) and the n=2 Volovik tracking law, with the V(q) parabola opening UPWARD."

    Definition 1: friction ODE  q″ + 3H q′ + V′(q) = 0    [substrate cosmological relaxation; q = Volovik
                  vacuum variable; 3H q′ = kinematic Hubble-friction term; V(q)=δρ_vac the a₀ response]
    Definition 2: V(q) = (1/2)·k_curv·(q − q*)² + const   [quadratic substrate potential; V′(q) = k_curv·(q − q*);
                  V″(q) = k_curv]   [k_curv from the 992 D_K eigenfrequencies; canonical_constants a_0_FW_zeta context]
    Definition 3: vacuum energy  rho_vac = ε(q) − μ q;  about q* the leading quadratic part is rho_vac ~ (q − q*)²
                  [Volovik q-theory; quadratic V => rho_vac ∝ q² (measured from q*)]
    Definition 4: tracking law  rho_vac ~ M_Pl² H^n  with n = 2  [Volovik Gibbs-Duhem, T.61:
                  n_eff = 2 + (GGE-pressure correction); session-66-mack-transit-workshop.md]

    Substitute (rho_vac two ways): quadratic V gives rho_vac ∝ (q − q*)²; tracking gives rho_vac ∝ H^n.
                  Equate:  (q − q*)² ∝ H^n.

    Simplify:
                  (q − q*)² ∝ H^n
                  (q − q*)   ∝ H^(n/2)
                  d ln(q − q*) / d ln H = n/2          [log-derivative of a power law]

    Canonical form:  slope ≡ d ln q / d ln H = n/2   (about the tracking fixed point q*).
                     At n = 2 (Volovik Gibbs-Duhem):  slope = 2/2 = 1   [Sage-exact: p = n/2, p|_{n=2} = 1].

    Direction (slope target):  slope = 1 EXACTLY on the attractor ⇒ PASS band |slope − 1| ≤ 0.05.
                     A computed slope > 1.05 or < 0.95 ⇒ the n=2 tracking law is NOT substrate-forced
                     (would require a free closure parameter ⇒ INFO/FAIL).

    Direction (k_curv sign / attractor existence):  the 3H q′ term is dissipative (overdamped friction).
                     A tracking ATTRACTOR at q* requires a RESTORING force V′(q) = k_curv·(q − q*) pointing
                     BACK toward q*, i.e. k_curv > 0  ⇔  V″(q*) = +|k_curv| = +3586.5  ⇔  parabola opens UPWARD.
                     If k_curv < 0 (concave, V″ = −3586.5), V′ pushes q AWAY from q* ⇒ q* is a repeller ⇒
                     friction cannot relax q onto the tracking law ⇒ slope diverges ⇒ FAIL by construction.
                     [Sage-verified: a convex/stable parabola (+|k_curv|) is the unique sign admitting a
                     friction attractor.] SIGN CONVENTION RESOLVED: k_curv = +3586.5.

    Conclusion: d ln q/d ln H = 1 is the substrate-forced attractor slope (set by the RATIO of the
                substrate restoring curvature k_curv>0 to the kinematic Hubble-friction factor 3H, with
                the n=2 Gibbs-Duhem tracking law fixing the exponent at n/2=1); the V(q) parabola opens
                UPWARD (k_curv=+3586.5). PASS iff this slope emerges UNFORCED within ±0.05.

# ---- Verdict rubric (3 fields) ----
PASS_meaning: >
  |d ln q/d ln H − 1.0| ≤ 0.05 emerges UNFORCED from the friction-ODE attractor (no slow-roll relation
  imposed, no free closure parameter) ⇒ the Volovik tracking exponent n=2 is substrate-FORCED ⇒ C10
  Object C DONE ⇒ the C10 DILUTION-CC discharge is UNCONDITIONAL ⇒ capstone §8.5 OPEN→CLOSED. The
  rho_vac ~ M_Pl² H² scaling is promoted from ASSUMED-PARTIALLY-PROVEN to a derived attractor of the
  substrate's own cosmological relaxation.
FAIL_meaning: >
  |d ln q/d ln H − 1.0| > 0.10 (info-band ceiling) OR the slope=1 result only arises by imposing the
  slow-roll quasi-static relation / a free closure parameter ⇒ n=2 is NOT a substrate-forced attractor ⇒
  C10 Object C remains underived ⇒ C10 stays ASSUMED-PARTIALLY-PROVEN, the DILUTION-CC discharge stays
  conditional, capstone §8.5 stays OPEN. (Composite collapses to FAIL also if regime_verdict==BREAKDOWN,
  e.g. the H(τ) backbone window is too short for a clean attractor regression — domain_used_frac<0.50.)
INFO_meaning: >
  0.05 < |d ln q/d ln H − 1.0| ≤ 0.10 (narrows toward n=2 but does not strictly hit the band), OR the
  attractor regression window is 5–50% shortened (regime_verdict=MARGINAL ⇒ composite INFO). C10 Object C
  is partially supported but not closed; §8.5 stays OPEN pending a cleaner backbone or window. Also the
  PRE-REG-INC mechanical-closure branch is reported as a FAIL line (value='PRE-REG-INC_blocked_by_…'),
  NOT INFO — see the W1→W2 decision point.

## §W2-2. S99-W2-BBN-RELIEF

> **`post-hoc:` correction (S99 W2-2 session-close — documentation-only per `v3-closure-recovery.md` PROHIBITED_ACTIONS Class-3; NO threshold/band/tolerance edited, verdict UNCHANGED).** The substitution-chain below writes the BBN-epoch lever as `relief_factor = X^{(n_eff−2)}` with `X = ln(H_BBN/H_0) = 40.2756` (→ 0.9223). That **double-logs X**. The substrate-correct lever is `relief_factor = (H_BBN/H_0)^{(n_eff−2)} = exp((n_eff−2)·X) = exp(−0.021889 · 40.2756) = 0.4141` — the form the S98 V.10 npz actually used, reproducing the canonical `frac_below = 0.474049` to 0 residual (baseline 1.1447 × 0.4141 = 0.4740). The executing W2-2 gate USED the correct `exp((n_eff−2)·X)` form (honest disclosure in WP §W2-2); the relief-*direction* logic ((n_eff−2)<0 ∧ X>0 ⇒ relief<1) holds under both forms, so `sign_verdict=PASS` is unaffected and the composite FAIL (magnitude-insufficient, Track B) stands. Secondary: the plan-pinned BBN bound `0.227113` is a rounded literal; the exact S66 `(7/8)·(4/11)^{4/3} = 0.227107` (drift 5.68e-6) is what the gate used. Surfaced by the W2-2 executor (`mack-cosmic-bridge`); recorded in `session-99-housekeeping.md §A`.
